Evelyn,

Thanks — we can meet the timeline. Proposed plan:

1) Produce a staged bundle (day-0) with all completed SIG answers exported to a single PDF (per evidence item), plus a manifest.csv and an evidence-index.pdf.
2) Run a PDF flatten + XMP stamping pass so each PDF is printable and portal-friendly (no incremental objects).
3) Upload into Whistic in two batches: controls (1..150) then attachments (supporting docs).

Filename convention I recommend (short + deterministic): HOLLIS_SIG_<YYYYMMDD>_<controlID>_<type>.pdf (e.g., HOLLIS_SIG_20270322_SC-08_evidence.pdf) — avoids spaces and special chars.

Manifest columns we will include: filename, control_id, control_text (short), checksum_sha256, file_size_bytes, page_count. Whistic accepts CSV with those columns.

OneTrust vs Whistic notes: Whistic prefers flattened PDFs and consistent filenames; OneTrust tolerates nested attachments but tends to choke on incremental PDF objects. For Whistic specifically, ensure no embedded portfolio files and max filename length < 120 chars.

I attached a starter bundle: SIG-responses-20270322.pdf and manifest.csv (sample).

If Marissa/Ben can run the flatten/stamp and then hand off to me for portal upload, we should be done by Thursday EOD. Can you confirm the required upload account/email we should use for the Whistic portal (team or individual)?

- Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-22T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Hollis SIG — flattening + manifest checklist

Marissa / Ben — please action the following today:

- Export evidence PDFs from our SIG tool as single-file PDFs per evidence reference.
- Run PDF flattening using the pipeline below (preserves timestamps and produces deterministic byte layout).
- Generate manifest.csv with columns: filename, control_id, checksum_sha256, file_size_bytes, page_count, source_doc_id.
- Produce evidence-index.pdf (1 page per attachment with short description and original filename).
- Add checksums to manifest and include a small README.txt with upload sequence (controls first, then attachments).

Suggested PDF flatten command (Linux container):

  # flatten + normalize
  qpdf --linearize in.pdf --replace-input && pdftk in.pdf output flat.pdf uncompress && gs -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -q -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dCompatibilityLevel=1.4 -sOutputFile=out_flat.pdf flat.pdf

Notes: the gs step removes incremental updates; pdftk ensures metadata fields get written consistently. If you hit fonts/embedding issues use ghostscript with -dSubsetFonts=false.

Also, add a checksum column using sha256sum and record it in manifest.csv. Whistic uses the checksum for verification during uploads.

Flag anything that requires redaction — we should not include raw PI in attachments without a redaction map.

Thanks,
- Markus

1) A handful (~6) of attachments are PDF/A (longform) and Ghostscript reported subset font warnings — I forced -dSubsetFonts=false, which increased size but kept rendering consistent.
2) One evidence item references a zipped attachment (logs_2026.zip). Whistic won’t accept embedded zips; we unpacked and split the log into grouped PDFs (logs_part1.pdf, logs_part2.pdf). We listed those in source_doc_id.

Attached: evidence-index.pdf (index with original filenames + short descriptions). Manifest is attached to this thread (manifest.csv).
